title: Eleven Winters and One Short Lamp
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（人与社会·科学与技术）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（人与社会·科学与技术）　|　核心词汇：engine　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 engine 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1932 my grandfather ① started an engine that no driver in the yard would have trusted, and he said the starting was the whole of the winter. The ② engine, meaning the machine itself and not the carriage, ran eleven winters and stayed untrusted in the book; an engine, he said, is the only thing in a yard that is judged by how long it is left untrusted.

Every ③ engine in that yard had the same short lamp beside it, and the ④ engine at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the spare and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An engine, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to trust; my grandfather said the trusting is the part that fills eleven winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the engine was the whole of the train, meaning the locomotive and not the machine. The ⑥ engine, meaning the locomotive and not any of that, is the only thing on a line that everybody waits for and nobody trusts; engine, he said, is either something you start or the only word that means both a machine and a locomotive. He said the locomotive is the part they remember.

By 1939 the ⑦ engine had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short lamp. The ⑧ engine of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in January, was one yard and eleven winters of trusting; engine, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to trust. He said the trusting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ engine I remember is the one trusted in the list, which closed in 1946 and is still described as the quietest in the yard. An ⑩ engine, my mother said in 1948, is the only one that improves by being trusted; every engine, she said, is a locomotive that has agreed to look like a machine. She said the locomotive was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 发动机；引擎（指院子里每一台旁边的那一台）
B. n. 引擎（指那台机器本身，与车厢相对）
C. 固定搭配：start an engine 发动引擎
D. n. 引擎（指留给备用车的那一台）
E. n. 引擎（抽象总称，指一支车队的动力之事）
F. n. 引擎（指清单上写到、被登记的那一台）
G. n. 机车；火车头（指线路上人人都等却无人信赖的那样东西）
H. n. 机车（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人信赖的那种力量）

items.q: started an engine that no driver in the yard would have trusted

answers.why: start an engine 意为“发动引擎”，1932 年祖父发动了一台院子里没有一位司机肯信赖的引擎。
engine 意为“引擎”，指那台机器本身而不是车厢，它经过了十一个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
engine 意为“引擎”，指院子里每一台旁边的那一台，每一台旁边都有同一盏短短的灯。
engine 意为“引擎”，指留给备用车的那一台，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
engine 意为“机车、火车头”，指线路上人人都等却无人信赖的那样东西，叔叔说这台机车就是那列火车的全部。
engine 意为“机车”，指人人都等却无人信赖的那种力量而不是那台机器，是线路上人人都等、却无人信赖的东西。
engine 意为“引擎”，指清单上写到、被登记的那一台，到 1939 年这一台成了清单里的一行。
engine 意为“引擎”，祖父一月写道，整件事的动力之事是一个院子和十一个冬天的信赖。
engine 意为“引擎”，我记得的是清单上登记的那一台，1946 年结束了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一台。
engine 为抽象总称，母亲 1948 年说，一台引擎是唯一会因为被好好信赖而变得更好的东西。
